div.head: Symbol (non meaning-bearing)
div.p: g (character or glyph) represents a non-standard character or glyph.

Where a symbol is non meaning-bearing, it should be represented using g[@ref]. The ref points to a glyph element in the charDecl section of the teiHeader which contains descrptive information about the glyph such as its name and character mappings that may be used to represent it. The TEI Guidelines chapter 5. Characters, Glyphs and Writing Modes provides a detailed explanation..
Note that in the past, many projects used type.
A Unicode character representing the symbol may also appear inside the g if desired.
The ref attribute in g can be used in various ways.

You may add this to your files, or include it as am extermal resource, as appropriate. The existing charDecl.xml file in the example stylesheets is used as a default where charDecl is not explicitly added in the XML file. The character mappings in this file can be resolved according to the parameters settings),
You mainatain this list of glyphs in an external file, in which case you will have to prepend a path to the charDecl.xml file in the g/@ref.

You can create shortcuts when using pointers to external files, as defined by the TEI prefixDef mechanism. If you define a prefix to be glyph, you may then use the following prefix definition, which maps your path to the prefix "glyph."

You may use external multiple sources, such as the EpiDoc charDecl.xml file together with a project specific file that defines missing symbols. Alternatively, you may contribute new symbols directly to the default charDecl in the stylesheet repository.
